name: Programming for Problem Solving Lab
sem: I or II (group-wise; alternative to Basic Mechanical Engineering Lab MEP-001)
objectives: Acquire knowledge about the basic concept of writing a program.
Understand the role of constants, variables, identifiers, operators, type conversion and other building blocks of C.
Use conditional expressions and looping statements to solve problems involving conditions and repetitions.
Use functions for modularity, and understand arrays and pointers for memory management.
Learn structures and unions through which derived data types can be formed.
outcomes: CO1 Acquire knowledge about the basic concept of writing a program.
CO2 Understand the role of constants, variables, identifiers, operators, type conversion and other building blocks of the C language.
CO3 Learn how to use conditional expressions and looping statements to solve problems associated with conditions and repetitions.
CO4 Understand the role of functions involving the idea of modularity, and understand the concept of arrays and pointers dealing with memory management.
CO5 Learn structures and unions through which derived data types can be formed.
text: C Programming and Data Structures, P.Padmanabham, Third Edition, BS Publications
Computer programming in C.V.RAjaraman, PHI Publishers.
C Programming, E.Balagurusamy, 3rd edition, TMH Publishers.
C Programming, M.V.S.S.N Venkateswarlu and E.V.Prasad,S.Chand Publishers
Mastering C,K.R.Venugopal and S.R.Prasad, TMH Publishers.
rule: All 12 programs (each with its a/b/c parts) are listed in the official table
note: Program numbering follows the official table (12 programs); each part is listed separately here.

exps.title: 1(a) Write a C program to find sum and average of three numbers
exps.aim: Read three numbers and print their sum and average.
exps.formula: sum = a + b + c ; avg = sum / 3 (use float, else integer division truncates)
viva: sum/3 with ints does integer division and drops the fractional part; a float (or 3.0) keeps it.
What does scanf need before a variable name?
The address-of operator &, e.g. scanf("%d",&a), so scanf can store the value at that address.

exps.title: 1(b) Write a C program to find the sum of individual digits of a given positiveinteger
exps.aim: Extract digits of a positive integer and add them.
viva: What does n/10 do for an int?

exps.title: 2(a) Write a C program to generate the first n terms of the Fibonacci sequence
exps.aim: Print first n Fibonacci numbers 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5 ...
viva: for/while loop running n times, updating two previous terms.
What are the first two terms?

exps.title: 2(b) Write a C program to generate prime numbers between 1 to n
exps.aim: List all primes up to n using divisibility tests.
exps.formula: i is prime if no d in 2..√i divides i (i ≥ 2)
viva: Why test divisors only up to √i?
If i has a factor larger than √i it must also have a smaller one, so checking up to √i is enough.
No; a prime has exactly two distinct divisors.

exps.title: 2(c) Write a C program to check if the given number is Armstrong or not
exps.aim: Check whether the sum of cubes of digits equals the number.
exps.formula: n is Armstrong (3-digit) if Σ digit³ = n, e.g. 153 = 1³+5³+3³
viva: For a k-digit number what power is used?
Each digit is raised to power k.

exps.title: 3(a) Write a C program to check whether the given number is perfect or not
exps.aim: Check if the sum of proper divisors equals the number.
exps.formula: perfect if Σ divisors d (d < n, n%d==0) = n, e.g. 6 = 1+2+3
viva: All proper divisors, i.e. excluding the number itself.

exps.title: 3(b) Write a C program to check whether the given number is strong or not
exps.aim: Check if the sum of factorials of digits equals the number.
exps.formula: strong if Σ (digit)! = n, e.g. 145 = 1!+4!+5!

exps.title: 4(a) Write a C program to find the roots of a quadratic equation
exps.aim: Find real/equal/complex roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 using the discriminant.
exps.apparatus: C compiler (GCC / Turbo C / Code::Blocks), math.h (sqrt)
exps.formula: D = b² − 4ac; x = (−b ± √D)/2a; D>0 real distinct, D=0 equal, D<0 complex
viva: The equation is linear, not quadratic; handle separately.

exps.title: 4(b) Write a C program perform arithmetic operations using switch statement
exps.aim: Perform +, −, *, / on two numbers chosen by a menu character.
exps.formula: switch(op){case '+': r=a+b; break; ... default: invalid}
viva: Why is break used in switch?
To stop fall-through into the next case.
No; the expression must be integral or char.

exps.title: 5(a) Write a C program to find factorial of a given integer using non-recursive function
exps.aim: Compute n! with a loop inside a user-defined function.
viva: Which data type is safe for large factorials?
unsigned long long; even this overflows beyond 20!.
A function written by the programmer with a return type, name and parameters.

exps.title: 5(b) Write a C program to find factorial of a given integer using recursive function
exps.aim: Compute n! by a function that calls itself.
exps.formula: fact(n) = n × fact(n−1), base case fact(0) = 1
viva: What happens without a base case?

exps.title: 6(a) Write C program to find GCD of two integers by using recursive function
exps.aim: Find GCD using Euclid's algorithm recursively.
exps.formula: gcd(a,b) = a if b == 0, else gcd(b, a mod b)

exps.title: 6(b) Write C program to find GCD of two integers by using non-recursive function
exps.aim: Find GCD using Euclid's algorithm with a loop.
exps.formula: while(b!=0){ t=b; b=a%b; a=t; } gcd = a
viva: No function-call overhead or stack growth.

exps.title: 7(a) Write a C program to find the largest and smallest number in a list of integers
exps.aim: Scan an array to find its maximum and minimum.
exps.formula: max = min = a[0]; for i=1..n-1: update if a[i] > max or a[i] < min
viva: It is a real element of the list, so the comparison is always valid.

exps.title: 7(b) Write a C program to Sort the Array in an Ascending Order
exps.aim: Sort n integers in ascending order (bubble/selection sort).
exps.formula: Bubble sort: repeatedly swap adjacent a[j] > a[j+1]; O(n²)
viva: How many passes does bubble sort need?

exps.title: 7(c) Write a C program to find whether the given matrix is symmetric or not
exps.aim: Check if a square matrix satisfies A = Aᵀ.
exps.formula: symmetric iff a[i][j] = a[j][i] for all i, j (square matrix only)
viva: Must a symmetric matrix be square?

exps.title: 8(a) Write a C program to perform addition of two matrices
exps.aim: Add two m×n matrices element by element.
exps.formula: C[i][j] = A[i][j] + B[i][j]; both must have the same order
viva: When can two matrices be added?
When they have the same number of rows and columns.
How is a 2-D array stored in C?

exps.title: 8(b) Write a C program using function to perform multiplication of two matrices
exps.aim: Multiply A(m×n) and B(n×p) using a function.
exps.formula: C[i][j] = Σk A[i][k]·B[k][j]; needs columns(A) = rows(B); three nested loops

exps.title: 9(a) Write a C program to use function to insert a sub-string in to given main stringfrom a given position
exps.aim: Insert a substring into a main string at position p.
exps.apparatus: C compiler (GCC / Turbo C / Code::Blocks), string.h
exps.formula: shift chars from p onward right by strlen(sub), then copy sub into the gap

exps.title: 9(b) Write a C program to swap the values of two variables using (i) Call by value (ii) Call by reference
exps.aim: Show that call by value does not swap, call by reference (pointers) does.
exps.formula: by reference: void swap(int *a,int *b){int t=*a;*a=*b;*b=t;} called as swap(&x,&y)
viva: Why does call by value fail to swap?
The function works on copies of the arguments.
How does C achieve call by reference?
By passing addresses and using pointers.

exps.title: 10(a) Write a C program using user-defined functions to determine whether the givenstring is palindrome or not
exps.aim: Check whether a string reads the same forwards and backwards.
exps.apparatus: C compiler (GCC / Turbo C / Code::Blocks), string.h
exps.formula: compare s[i] with s[len−1−i] for i < len/2

exps.title: 10(b) Write a C program that displays the position or index in the main string Swhere the sub string T begins, or - 1 if S doesn't contain T
exps.aim: Find first occurrence of substring T in S (naive search).
exps.apparatus: C compiler (GCC / Turbo C / Code::Blocks), string.h
exps.formula: for each i, compare S[i..i+m−1] with T; return i on match, else −1

exps.title: 11(a) Write C program to count the number of lines, words and characters in a giventext
exps.aim: Count lines, words and characters in an input text.
exps.formula: chars++ per char; lines++ on '\n'; words++ when a non-space follows a space/newline/tab
viva: How do you detect a word boundary?
A transition from whitespace to a non-whitespace character.

exps.title: 11(b) Write a C program to find the sum of integer array elements using pointers
exps.aim: Traverse an array with a pointer and add elements.
exps.formula: sum += *(p + i), where p = a (base address); a[i] ≡ *(a+i)
viva: What does the array name denote?
The address of its first element.
What does p++ do for an int pointer?
Moves it by sizeof(int) bytes to the next element.

exps.title: 12(a) Write a C Program to Calculate Total and Percentage marks of a student usingstructure
exps.aim: Store student data in a struct and compute total and percentage.
exps.formula: total = m1+m2+...+mn ; percentage = total × 100 / (n × max marks)
viva: A user-defined type grouping variables of different types under one name.
Dot (.) for variables, arrow (->) for pointers.

exps.title: 12(b) Write a program to open and read a file using file handling
exps.aim: Open a text file, read its contents and display them.
exps.formula: FILE *fp = fopen(name,"r"); while((ch=fgetc(fp))!=EOF) putchar(ch); fclose(fp);
viva: What does fopen return on failure?
To flush buffers and release the file handle.
